findings.description: The function's environment block embeds a literal AWS access key ID and secret access key (access_key / secret_key). These are stored in plaintext in the Terraform source and state, are visible in the Lambda console, and are retrievable by any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, giving an attacker directly usable long-lived AWS credentials. The function already has an execution role and should use its ambient role credentials instead.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables, which in this configuration carry secret credential material, are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key. There is no key policy boundary or independent CloudTrail key-usage audit trail restricting who can decrypt the secrets.

The function runs on nodejs12.x, which is past end-of-life in AWS Lambda and upstream Node.js. It no longer receives security patches, leaving known vulnerabilities in the runtime and its bundled OpenSSL/libuv components unaddressed.
